title: Wise Words
subtitle: WITH MARCO REYES  ·  STORY NIGHT

segments.head: TONIGHT: BONNIE'S DINER
segments.author: Wise Words
lines: Good evening, everyone.
I'm Marco Reyes, and this is Wise Words.
Tonight's story is about Bonnie Ames, who runs a little diner in Rapid City, South Dakota.
For thirty years, she's flipped pancakes for truckers and ranchers.
Then a stranger with a phone ate a short stack, and wrote a review.

segments.head: CHAPTER 1: ONE STAR
segments.quote: Love your enemies, for they tell you your faults.
segments.author: Benjamin Franklin
lines: The review said: One star. The pancakes taste like coasters.
Bonnie was so mad she flipped an omelet onto the floor.
Then she saw the Ben Franklin line her dad had taped by the register:
Love your enemies, for they tell you your faults.
So she ate a pancake, slowly. Flat. Dry. He was right.

segments.head: CHAPTER 2: GRANDMA'S CARD
segments.quote: It is impossible for a man to learn what he thinks he already knows.
segments.author: Epictetus
lines: For years, she'd used a cheap mix. She was sure she knew pancakes.
Her cook Lupe quoted Epictetus, an old Greek thinker:
It is impossible for a man to learn what he thinks he already knows.
So Bonnie dug out her grandma's recipe card. Real buttermilk.
At sixty-one, she started over like a beginner.

segments.head: CHAPTER 3: THE BAD WEEK
segments.quote: The art of life is more like the wrestler's art than the dancer's.
segments.author: Marcus Aurelius
lines: The first batches were a disaster. One pancake stuck to the ceiling.
Then the grill died, and a blizzard closed the highway.
Her brother Dale, a retired wrestling coach, read her the Roman emperor Marcus Aurelius:
The art of life is more like the wrestler's art than the dancer's.
So she cooked on a borrowed camp stove and kept the doors open.

segments.head: CHAPTER 4: THE LONG LINE
segments.quote: The reward of a thing well done is to have done it.
segments.author: Ralph Waldo Emerson
lines: By spring, the pancakes were tall and fluffy, and the line went out the door.
Lupe said, let's go back to the mix. It's faster.
Bonnie pointed to the Emerson line chalked on the menu board:
The reward of a thing well done is to have done it.
So every pancake got made the slow way. Nobody left.

segments.head: CHAPTER 5: THE CRITIC
segments.quote: Everybody is ignorant, only on different subjects.
segments.author: Will Rogers
lines: Then the stranger came back. His name was Tyler, and he looked nervous.
In the kitchen, Tyler admitted he couldn't even boil an egg.
Bonnie laughed, and quoted the cowboy humorist Will Rogers:
Everybody is ignorant, only on different subjects.
Then she taught him to flip a pancake. The third one landed on the plate.

segments.head: CHAPTER 6: THE FRAME
segments.quote: Gratitude is the sign of noble souls.
segments.author: Aesop
lines: Tyler's new review: five stars. She didn't just feed me. She made me a cook.
But Bonnie framed the one-star review instead.
Underneath, she wrote a line from Aesop, the ancient storyteller:
Gratitude is the sign of noble souls.
Now the Tyler Special is on the menu. Not one pancake is a coaster.

segments.head: THAT'S TONIGHT'S STORY
segments.quote: Hear the critic. Unlearn. Wrestle. Do it well. Stay humble. Say thanks.
segments.author: Marco Reyes
lines: That's tonight's story.
Hear the critic. Unlearn. Wrestle through bad weeks. Do it well. Stay humble. Say thank you.
I once got a one-star review from my own wife. For my singing. She was right.
I'm Marco Reyes. Good night.
